scope: Apply to newly written or modified first-party code. Exclude generated and third-party code; avoid unrelated formatting changes.
basis: Project defaults adapted from the official references below; this is not a claim of full upstream compliance.
precedence: Explicit project conventions and existing formatter/linter configuration
documentation_language: Use the project's established language for code comments and API documentation; default to Chinese when unspecified. The English language of this specification does not require English comments. Preserve verbatim evidence and quotations.

design: Keep functions focused and control flow readable; avoid speculative abstractions and hidden side effects.
Reuse existing modules and standard libraries; explain the need for new dependencies.
Validate untrusted input at boundaries and keep business rules separate from external I/O where useful.
naming: Use domain-specific names and consistent terminology; avoid unexplained abbreviations and magic values.
Names and types must make units, mutability and important ownership constraints clear.
comments: Explain non-obvious reasons, invariants, algorithms, compatibility workarounds and concurrency constraints near the relevant code.
Do not narrate obvious statements or add comments merely to satisfy a count or length quota.
Update or remove stale comments in the same change as the behavior they describe; remove commented-out dead code.
Write TODO(owner-or-issue): actionable follow-up. Supply a real owner or existing issue reference; never invent identifiers.
Every lint/type-check suppression or unsafe operation needs a local explanation of necessity and applicable safety conditions.
Comments and examples must not contain credentials, sensitive production data or unsupported claims.
api_documentation: Document public/exported APIs and module entrypoints; document private helpers when their contracts or behavior are non-obvious.
State purpose, parameter meaning and constraints, result semantics and failure conditions; omit sections that do not apply.
Describe applicable units, nullability, ownership, mutation, side effects, cancellation and thread-safety guarantees.
Keep caller-facing contracts beside declarations and implementation reasoning beside implementation code.
Do not repeat types already expressed by the language. Keep examples minimal, accurate and executable when practical.
Generated declarations, accurate inherited documentation and obvious trivial accessors may omit redundant documentation.
error_handling: Handle errors explicitly or propagate them with useful context; never silently convert failure into success.
Release resources predictably and bound retries, timeouts and background work according to the operation contract.
Logs must preserve useful failure context without exposing secrets; avoid duplicate logging of the same propagated error.
testing: Cover changed behavior, regressions and important boundaries with meaningful assertions rather than restating implementation.
Keep tests deterministic; distinguish isolated tests, integration evidence and real-environment acceptance.
Run the project checks relevant to the change and report actual results, failures and skipped coverage.
Synchronize affected API documentation, examples and operational guidance with behavior changes.

documentation: Use //! for crate/module documentation and /// for public items.
Include applicable Examples, Errors, Panics and Safety sections; keep examples suitable for doctests.
Unsafe APIs must explain caller obligations; unsafe blocks need local SAFETY comments establishing their invariants.
rules: Use existing rustfmt configuration and preserve import groups.
Express recoverable failures with Result; handle or propagate errors with ?.
Avoid unjustified unwrap/expect in business paths; explain intentional panic conditions.
Keep ownership and borrowing explicit; do not introduce unsafe solely to bypass borrow checking.

sources.title: Google JavaScript Style Guide
sources.note: Upstream is no longer updated. These JavaScript defaults do not require a TypeScript migration.

documentation: Use JSDoc for public/exported APIs; describe parameters, return values and thrown or rejected errors.
Use type tags when useful in untyped JavaScript, following existing tooling.
Use ordinary comments for implementation reasoning; keep JSDoc next to its declaration.
rules: Prefer const; use let for reassignment and do not introduce var.
Use strict equality by default and avoid surprising implicit coercion.
Respect existing module configuration; prefer ES modules when supported.
Handle asynchronous failures; do not create implicit globals or mutate built-in prototypes.

sources.title: Google Shell Style Guide
sources.note: Upstream targets Bash. Bash-only syntax must not be introduced into POSIX sh scripts.

documentation: Add a file-header purpose comment after the shebang.
Document library functions and non-obvious functions: purpose, Globals, Arguments, Outputs and Returns as applicable.
Describe exit-status meanings and destructive effects; explain surprising quoting or portability requirements.
rules: Declare the actual shell dialect; use local only when supported.
Quote expansions and forward arguments with "$@"; prefer $(...) over backticks.
Use Bash arrays or POSIX positional arguments for lists; avoid eval and command-string assembly.
Check important command/pipeline failures, write errors to stderr and use the correct ShellCheck dialect.
